#Architecture

How Wren is put together, and the rules that keep it from breaking as it grows. For the overview, the build and the feature list, see the README.

#The rules that keep it from breaking at scale

  1. One ownership tree. process → tab → navigation → page → (instances, DOM, requests, timers). Everything a page starts is registered in its scope (src/base/scope.odin); closing a tab or navigating is scope_close. Cleanups run newest first, children before parents, so nothing outlives what it points to. Scopes are main-thread only.
  2. Handles, never pointers, cross boundaries. Handle = generation << 32 | index, 0 is invalid. A destroyed or recycled slot fails to resolve. Late network events, timers and listener callbacks for dead objects are dropped, not delivered to reused memory. Pool objects never move (chunked), so ^T stays valid until removed.
  3. Single UI thread, everything else posts. The network stack's threads, the image decoders, the layout and style threads and the blocking pool only push events and host.post back to the loop; every user-visible callback runs on the loop thread. The DOM and the Wasm instances of a page live on the UI thread (workers have their own store).
  4. Mechanism and policy are separate. net moves bytes and never follows a redirect, stores a cookie or sends ambient credentials. fetch decides, per hop, on the UI thread, with the document's Environment in hand. A guest, a module load and a navigation all go through the same code, so there is one place where "may this request happen" is answered.
  5. Bounded everything, with a reason each. Per-host (6) and global (256) request limits in our own priority queues (so waiting never counts against connect timeouts); reading pauses when 1 MB is queued for a request; max_body caps a response; at most 20 redirects (the Fetch Standard's number); cookies: at most 180 per site and 3000 in total with LRU eviction; at most 1000 preflight cache entries; guest memory is capped; every host → guest call has a deadline (epoch interruption; polls of its own in the JavaScript engine, src/wasm/poll.odin): a spinning script is stopped, the instance lives on. Every one of these numbers is a preference (about:config).
  6. The guest cannot reach host memory. Every address + length pair of an import is checked by its generated trampoline against the guest's linear memory before our code runs; strings are copied out through caller-provided buffers.
  7. No recursion on hostile depth. Tree destruction, text extraction, searches and the HTML replay are iterative.
  8. Everything is configurable. Each package declares its preferences in a settings.odin (config.Def: dotted lower-case name, description, type, bounds, unit) and reads them through settings_from_prefs; the shell registers every table (src/browser/settings.odin) and src/browser/prefs_test.odin checks that each one is well formed.
  9. State lives with what owns it. See below: what is one App's is not a global.
  10. Layers point one way. A tool (src/tools) may import the product; the product never imports wb:tools/*. What both need is a package of src: crash reports (src/crashtrace), the stacks of another process (src/stacks), the test environment (src/testenv). Only a *_windows.odin file imports core:sys/windows, and a neutral struct holds no Win32 type (portability.md). A package links only what its users need: URLPattern is src/urlpattern, so the users of src/url (cookies, CSP, WebAuthn) do not link the regular expression engine. src/tools/test_all/lint_layers.odin checks the imports.
  11. The profile's files have one writer. host.File_Writer (src/host/profile_file.odin, App.writer) writes every file of the profile, for the shell and for the pages (Storage_Manager.writer, Blocker.writer). Its owner makes the text on its own thread, only when what the file holds changed, and calls host.profile_write or host.profile_remove (a host.Profile_File when it keeps one; host.profile_post from another thread). The blocking pool writes the file whole and atomically (a temporary file renamed over it), one write of a file at a time: only the newest text waits. A failed write is logged and tried again later and later, and the user is told once. At exit profile_files_flush writes what waits, and every later text is written at once. A job that does more than give a whole text (the cookies' copy, the history's journal, the crash snapshot) calls host.file_put, file_append, file_move or file_drop on a worker. In the check build these panic on the interface thread while the pool could do the write. src/tools/test_all/lint_file_writes.odin fails on another direct write in src: tools/file_writes_allowed.txt lists the ones left (diagnostics, the user's own files, the stores with their own format), each with why.

#Where state lives

The aim is several Apps (browser.App: one browser, its profile, its loop, its windows) in one process, each on a thread of its own, so that tests run side by side in one binary. An App runs on one thread, the one that runs its loop (app_start's); its page thread works for it. So a global is allowed only for what it is, and tools/globals_allowed.txt gives every global of src/browser, src/page, src/style, src/layout, src/media and src/js its class (src/tools/test_all/lint_globals.odin fails on a new one, a gone one, or a class the code contradicts):

  • const: a table, written by the compiler or once (a sync.Once) before anything reads it. Any thread reads it.
  • process: a resource there is one of whatever the number of Apps: the Wasm engine, a thread pool, a library of the system, the single-instance channel, an id unique in the process (atomic). Locked, atomic, or bound to a thread the note names.
  • thread: @(thread_local), and only then (the lint holds the class to the attribute both ways). In packages that have no App (page, style, layout), what is one App's is its thread's: the live pages, the navigables, the frames waiting to close (page/web.odin, page/frames.odin), page.the_pages. In browser, what the thread that paints keeps (the compositor's layers, the planes, the canvas text's glyphs) and the_app, the App of this thread.
  • test: a test's own.

There is no class for one App's state (nor one window's, tab's or page's): it is a field of App, Browser_Window.own, Tab or Page, and the lint fails on a global that is none of the above.

What belongs to the App is a field of App (src/browser/main.odin), reached through the ^App the code is given. A callback the App sets up carries it: a timer's or a watch's data, a job's struct (Setup_Job.app), a window subclass's reference data (app_commands_windows.odin). the_app is what is left for code that has no ^App yet, mostly hooks of other packages (page.Embedder_Hooks, the canvas' text engine), the painting code and the developer tools' drawing: a thread of its own sees nil.

What the App's pages share is page.Pages (src/page/pages.odin, App.pages): the embedder's hooks, the image cache, the script compile service, the style threads, the profile's stores (Cache API, file system, service workers, Web Locks, storage buckets, storage access decisions), the message ports, the shared workers, the statistics. The page package reaches it through page.the_pages, bound by page.bind to the threads that run the App's pages: its loop's (app_start), its page thread's (page_thread.odin), a worker's (worker_main, its creator's), a compile thread's. A program that embeds pages without the shell (src/tools/headless, the web tests, apiconformance) binds its own; a page test binds one with test_pages(t).

What the Apps of the process share is set up by the first App to start and let go of by the last to end (src/browser/process_share.odin: one atomic word, the Apps that use it or a busy mark while the first sets it up or the last lets it go; whoever starts or ends meanwhile waits on it): the Wasm engine and its host functions, the bytecode cache, the image decoders, the layout threads, the decoded web fonts, the crash session (page.process_shutdown). The first App's preferences and profile configure them.

src/tools/e2e/two_apps.odin runs two Apps, each on a thread of its own, at once: each sees only its own tabs, pages, storage, channel messages and frame, and nothing of either is left once both have stopped. The toolkit keeps the interface state it draws with in one variable of the process (ext/gui_toolkit/src/ui/state.odin, g): until it is the thread's (@(private, thread_local) g: ^State), the two Apps' own threads take turns between the test's meetings (what they run besides runs at once); with that one change they run at once too.

#Wasm engine

Wasmtime, the official C API release v49.0.3, downloaded by wrentool fetch wasmtime (version and SHA-256 pinned in the script) into build\wasmtime; the static wasmtime.lib is linked into the exe (no DLL; it adds about 12 MB). It needs ws2_32 advapi32 userenv ntdll shell32 ole32 bcrypt kernel32 and the C runtime, linked in as for every native library of Wren (libcmt libucrt libvcruntime, the static C runtime that Odin's core:c/libc is: wren.exe needs no runtime DLL), declared in src/wasm/wasmtime.odin. Modules are compiled by Cranelift (or Winch, wasm.wasmtime.compiler), kept in a memory cache and in an HMAC-authenticated disk cache of the profile (wasm-cache); the JavaScript engine's image is not compiled on the user's machine at all: its machine code is made at build time and shipped in wren.exe (src/wasm/shipped.odin, jsengine precompile), with the disk cache's path behind it when it does not fit (a changed wasm.wasmtime.* preference, a CPU without its features). Every call from the host has a wall-clock deadline (wasm.max_call_ms, epoch interruption; the JavaScript engine's image runs on a second Wasmtime engine without epoch checks and polls at the head of its loops, src/wasm/poll.odin; with wasm.wasmtime.fuel, also an instruction budget). src/tools/wasmbench compares the compiler configurations and measures host calls.

#The web API: one description, everything generated

Every Wasm import of the browser is described once, in api/*.widl (a dialect of Web IDL: modules, functions, typed handles, enums, flags, structs, callbacks, raises, [Exposed=Window|Worker], documentation). src/tools/bindgen generates from it, deterministically:

  • the host side, src/page/api_generated.odin: one trampoline per import, defined directly on the Wasmtime linker, which checks every address against the module's memory, converts strings (UTF-8 checked), handles (looked up by kind), enums, flags and structs, and calls the implementation (bindings_*.odin) with Odin values. The expected prototype of each implementation is written above its trampoline: a missing or mistyped one does not compile;
  • the Odin guest SDK, sdk/odin/<package>/<module>.odin, the wren collection (import "wren:dom"; distinct handle types, string / []u8 / Maybe, (T, Error) results, F / F_len / F_alloc for strings of unknown size);
  • the documentation, docs/api/ (with the ABI);
  • conformance tests: examples/apiconformance and src/tools/apiconformance/cases_generated.odin (bad addresses, bad UTF-8, dead handles, enums out of range, buffers too small, for every function).

build.bat regenerates what changed; test_all fails when a generated file is out of date (bindgen -check). Imports take 64-bit addresses in a module whose memory 0 is memory64 (wasm.features.memory64).

A document names its modules with <script type="application/wasm" src="..." nonce="...">, any number of them. They are fetched concurrently and run in document order, each in its own instance sharing the DOM. (The syntax is one function, html.wasm_scripts, if it ever changes.)

#JavaScript

JavaScript is one more Wasm guest, not a second engine beside Wasm. The engine is written in Odin (src/engine): a front-end that compiles source to QuickJS-ng 0.17 bytecode, the interpreter (jsrt, with a hot loop of its own and a loop JIT that compiles hot loops and hot functions to Wasm at run time: numbers, properties guarded by shapes, small callees inlined, compiled functions called directly, natives and getters called, objects and strings made; engine/jit.md), and the numeric, Unicode, regexp and date libraries. jscapi gives it the QuickJS C API, which the glue (native/js/odin, all Odin) is written against; the web platform's objects are hand-written members plus bindings generated from the Web IDL of webref (src/tools/bindgen, package jsgen, into native/js/odin/bindings_gen.odin). src\tools\buildjs compiles it all to one wasm32 module (Odin, linked by Odin's own wasm-ld (on Linux, lld's), no C library: no C of ours is compiled) and pre-initializes it at build time (src/wasm/preinit.odin: interfaces, prototypes and preludes already built in the memory image); the image is embedded in the exe (src/js/image). Each page and each JavaScript worker gets its own instance (a realm), whose imports are the same api/*.widl functions Wasm pages use, plus js*.widl for what only the engine needs. So the limits of every guest apply: Wasmtime's sandbox, the memory cap, epoch interruption (wasm.max_call_ms), on top of the engine's own (javascript.max_heap_bytes, javascript.slow_script_ms). A trap loses the realm (the status bar says JS stopped), never the browser. Wrappers hold their DOM nodes; wrappers of one DOM tree are grouped at each collection so that a detached tree nothing holds is freed (src/page/js_realm.odin). Script loading (src/page/js_load*.odin) follows HTML's processing model. Details: native/js/README.md; coverage: docs/js/coverage.md.

#Image and font decoders

src/images decodes on its own threads, never on the interface thread. Every format but HEIF is decoded by the crate native\media, part of Wren's one Rust static library (see "The Rust library" below), the same on every system; HEIF goes through the platform (WIC, when the Store codec is installed), and images.decode.system_codecs hands PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, ICO and TIFF to WIC as before (src/images/parity_test_windows.odin compares both on every fixture):

  • PNG / APNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, ICO, TIFF: image 0.25.10 (png, zune-jpeg, gif, tiff; native/media/src/raster.rs): EXIF orientation, ICC profiles, GIF and APNG animation composed by the decoder, the ICO entry that fits the size shown; PNG and JPEG encoding for the canvas.
  • SVG: resvg 0.48.1 (usvg + tiny-skia; text with the system fonts through fontdb). Rendered at the size it is shown at (device pixels), in the secure static mode of SVG images (no external resource, script or animation); hostile documents are bounded by images.svg.* (nodes, depth, entity and <use> expansion, rendering cost). Inline <svg> elements of HTML documents are drawn by the same renderer (src/page/inline_svg.odin); the HTML of their <foreignObject> elements is laid out and painted by Wren's own layout, in the SVG's coordinate space: the viewBox mapping, nested <svg> viewports and the transforms around it, its <clipPath>s (user space or bounding box units) and the viewports of the nested <svg>s it is in (unless overflow: visible), intersected, as a polygon clip, the filters of it and its ancestors: filter functions, and <filter>s whose primitives chain blurs, feColorMatrix saturate / hueRotate and a linear feComponentTransfer as blur(), saturate(), hue-rotate(), brightness() (src/layout/foreign_object.odin). The picture is drawn in parts split at the foreign objects, so that shapes drawn after one cover it (Svg_Parts). An inline <svg> clips to its viewport (svg:not(:root) { overflow: hidden }). Not yet: <filter>s of other primitives (offsets, floods, merges, colour matrices).
  • WebP: image-webp 0.2.4 (pure safe Rust: lossy, lossless, alpha, animation).
  • AVIF: zenavif-parse 0.6.2 (container: alpha, grids, sequences, colr / irot / imir / clap) + rav1d 1.1.0 (the Rust port of dav1d, with dav1d's assembly: NASM 2.16.03 is fetched and checked by SHA-256 by the script).
  • Colour: qcms 0.3.0 (Firefox's): ICC profiles of every format, AVIF's CICP code points and EXIF's Adobe RGB to sRGB (images.color_management).
  • WOFF2 web fonts: brotli-decompressor 6.1.0, then the glyf / loca / hmtx transforms reversed (native/media/src/woff2.rs, used by src/webfont).

Every crate is pinned (see below). wrentool gen media-fixtures (ImageMagick, FFmpeg) made the AVIF / WebP test files of examples\site\media; src\tools\mediabench times decodes.

#The Rust library (native/)

A program links one Rust static library at most: each carries its own copy of Rust's standard library, and two built by the same compiler define the same symbols. So all of Wren's Rust code is one Cargo workspace, native/, with one Cargo.lock, one target directory (build\native\target) and one output, build\native\wren_native.lib (wrentool build native, run by build.bat; nothing is done when build\native\STAMP matches the sources):

  • native/media (crate wren_media, a library): the image decoders and WOFF2 above (src/images, src/webfont).
  • native/net (crate wren_net): the network stack (src/net/rust.odin, see "Network" below).
  • The toolkit's crates, path dependencies that stay in the toolkit: ext/gui_toolkit/native/text (gt_text, the native text backend; feature text, left out of a WREN_TEXT=dwrite build) and ext/gui_toolkit/native/a11y (gt_a11y, AccessKit; feature a11y). The toolkit is built with -define:FONT_NATIVE_LINK=false -define:A11Y_NATIVE_LINK=false: it links nothing of its own.
  • native/wren_native, the assembly crate (a staticlib with no code): it picks the libraries, and their C functions (wm_*, wn_*, gt_*) are exported from it.

Two Cargo profiles, with the same code generation for each crate (opt-level = 3, one codegen unit, panic = "unwind": every entry point catches panics):

  • release (build.bat release and profile: what is shipped, and measured as shipped): fat LTO, the whole graph optimized as one module. A change in any crate runs that step again over all of them (a minute or more).
  • quick (build.bat, debug, check, the CI): no LTO, each crate's objects go into the archive as they are. A change in one crate rebuilds that crate and the archive: touching the accessibility adapter recompiles neither the decoders nor the text backend (7 s against 65 s). Measured against release on 2026-10-27: decoding as fast (WebP, AVIF, SVG, WOFF2 within 3 %), shaping 2 to 5 % slower, the exe 0.6 MB larger.

Both stay compiled in build\native\target; switching between them copies the library. The CI caches the compiled crates by profile and Cargo.lock (.github/actions/setup): a run whose Cargo.lock did not change compiles only the workspace's and the toolkit's crates.

Why not a DLL per library (cdylib): measured, the adapter's DLL is 0.6 MB and the text backend's 2.4 MB (each with its own standard library), loading one costs 2 to 3 ms (40 ms the first time a new file is scanned), and each DLL is one more file to sign, ship and keep in step with the exe; wren.exe needs no file beside it, and stays so.

Every crate is pinned by exact version in its Cargo.toml and by SHA-256 in native\Cargo.lock (--locked); wrentool gen rust-crates writes the list about:licenses shows (native\rust-crates.txt). Wasmtime's library carries a standard library of another compiler: its mangled symbols differ, and the one unmangled symbol both define (rust_eh_personality, unused on MSVC) is renamed in ours with llvm-objcopy.

#Network

Package net is the transport: queues per priority, per-host and global limits, throttling (DevTools), generational handles, scopes, back-pressure, the Headers / Data / Done / Failed events, WebSockets' state machine. Under it, one of two stacks (network.backend, overridden by the WREN_NET_BACKEND environment variable):

  • rust (the default): native/net, the same on every platform. tokio threads of its own; hyper-util's pooled client over our connector (the system resolver, TCP attempts staggered by 250 ms, the system proxy: environment, Windows registry, macOS configuration, with a CONNECT tunnel for https and WebSockets), HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 by ALPN; rustls (ring) with rustls-platform-verifier: the system's trust store and policy, plus network.tls.extra_ca_file; gzip, deflate and Brotli decoded as the body streams; WebSockets on tungstenite over an HTTP/1.1 upgrade. HTTP/3 (quinn + h3) for an origin that announced it (Alt-Svc): the request that opens the QUIC connection waits for it network.http3.race_ms at most, then goes over TCP; the others use QUIC only once it is up; an origin where QUIC failed is left to TCP for network.http3.broken_host_ms. Results wait in the library's queue; one notification per burst posts net's drain to the loop, which takes them one by one (wn_net_poll) and copies what it keeps: no allocation of ours on a library thread, no memory of the library freed by us. Proxy auto-configuration scripts (PAC) are not run: where the system proxy names one, the client uses WinHTTP.
  • winhttp: WinHTTP's asynchronous mode (Windows only). Never HTTP/3: WinHTTP does not fall back to TCP where QUIC does not get through.

Errors keep WinHTTP's numbers (12002 timeout, 12007 name, 12029 connect, 12030 lost, 12152 invalid answer, 12175 / 12037 / 12038 / 12045 certificates with WinHTTP's secure flags) whichever stack ran the request. src/tools/e2e/web_net.odin runs the transport on both; WREN_NET_BACKEND=rust|winhttp makes a web test run by hand use one.

#Security model

  • Origins. scheme://host:port, or an opaque origin equal only to itself (file:, data:, redirect-tainted requests). Sites use the Public Suffix List (github.io is a suffix; localhost and IPs have no registrable domain).
  • Requests carry an Environment: Request_Desc.initiator is the document asking (nil = the address bar). Modes: navigate, same-origin, no-cors (opaque response: status 0, no headers, no body for scripts) and cors.
  • CORS: Origin header, ACAO / ACAC checks, header exposure filtering, preflights with the spec's rules (safelisted methods and headers, * never covering Authorization, wildcard disabled with credentials), preflight cache with max-age. Cross-origin Wasm modules need CORS; modules must be application/wasm.
  • Cookies: stored and sent only by fetch (WinHTTP's are off). Secure needs a secure context (localhost counts), __Secure- / __Host- prefixes, SameSite (default Lax, None needs Secure), HttpOnly invisible to scripts, "leave Secure cookies alone", Domain checked against the PSL. Third-party cookies are allowed by default (privacy.third_party_cookies, Chromium's default: SameSite applies, and they are partitioned per top-level site, storage.partitioned). document.cookie exists only for tuple origins.
  • HSTS, referrer policy (header, <meta>, per request), mixed content (blocked; images auto-upgraded), bad ports, Fetch Metadata headers (Sec-Fetch-*), CSP (headers and <meta>, report-only, upgrade-insecure-requests, block-all-mixed-content; script-src governs Wasm modules, worker-src workers).
  • Local files: a file: document may read files in its own directory tree and nothing else; web pages never read local files; only the address bar may open any file.

#Web Authentication (passkeys)

src/webauthn is the client of Web Authentication Level 3 without the page: the options in their standard JSON form (what a server sends, what navigator.credentials.create() / get() serialize a dictionary to), the RP ID (a registrable domain suffix of the document's domain, Public Suffix List of src/url), the exact bytes of clientDataJSON, the ceremony timeout, extensions, toJSON(), and CBOR / COSE for getPublicKey() (DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo). The authenticators are the operating system's, behind an interface (Platform): on Windows webauthn.dll (Windows Hello, security keys, a phone over hybrid, the passkey managers Windows knows), loaded on first use and used up to the API version the system has; its dialog belongs to the browser's window. A software authenticator (virtual.odin, ES256 through BCrypt, keys in memory) replaces it for automated tests only. src/page/bindings_webauthn.odin adds the page's conditions (secure context, a recent click or key press, the tab shown in the focused window, one ceremony at a time) and runs the blocking platform call on a thread of its own; the window stays responsive and draws nothing while the user answers, the address bar shows a chip (click: cancel). Aborts, the lifetime timer and the page closing cancel the system's operation; if the system does not give it back within security.webauthn.cancel_grace_ms, the page is answered anyway and the exit does not wait for it. Nothing about credentials is logged.

#Rendering pipeline

DOM mutations and style changes are journaled (src/dom/journal.odin, src/style/journal.odin). A frame runs, as needed: the style pass (full, in parallel on large documents, or a partial restyle from invalidation sets), the layout pass (refresh, incremental or full; layout.incremental.verify checks an incremental pass against a full one), the display list, then the compositor (src/browser/compositor.odin), which records the display list into retained pictures of the toolkit's draw layer and replays them every frame: scrolling and transform animations only change matrices. The painter (src/browser/render.odin) maps the display list onto draw's transform, clip and layer stacks (filters, blend modes, backdrops, masks). Frames are paced on the display's refresh by the toolkit's cadence model (platform/pacing.odin, its docs/pacing.md: one decision per frame), which src/browser/pacing.odin executes.
